classificationReport.head: 96d39ed
evidenceConsulted: reports/stable-staker/17/invariants/invariant-results.json (INV-1..INV-6; 640,640 Foundry calls + 302,817 Medusa calls; non-vacuity tripwire PASS)

bindingConstraintsApplied.N24_4c: 'Nothing in the protocol's safety argument may depend on antimatter being unobtainable while the flag is false.' NO finding's severity was discounted on the grounds that claimEnabled is closed. Verified per finding in `n24_4c_compliance`. Note the converse: 4(c) is a refusal to let the gate act as a mitigation; it does not convert the gate's own porosity into an impact, because by the project's own construction nothing depends on it.
bindingConstraintsApplied.v2SuppressionsVoid: The minter-cushion and externally-derived-yield/opportunity-cost suppressions are VOID for V2: V2 Antimatter is redeemable into unbacked phUSD, so destroyed or prematurely-delivered Antimatter is real value. Applied affirmatively at DEDUP-004 (destruction => real loss). NOT used to manufacture impact at DEDUP-001, where conservation is exact and no incremental Antimatter exists.
bindingConstraintsApplied.law3: Owner trusted for KNOWING actions. No malicious-owner rating appears in this run. Two NON-OBVIOUS footguns (DEDUP-001, DEDUP-004) are classified by the impact they unlock, per the surprise test, and are not discounted as centralization.
bindingConstraintsApplied.law2: Five findings carry `faithfulness: true` and are routed to spec-conformance.md as F-XX at honest severity. None is buried in the QA/gas bundle.
bindingConstraintsApplied.preDeployment: V2 has zero broadcast records on any chain. `claimEnabled == false` is the DEPLOYMENT DEFAULT (:100), so every gate-conditioned finding describes the shipped state on day one. No finding was discounted as not-yet-live.

classifiedFindings.title: The claimEnabled gate is fully bypassable in two ordinary transactions: withdraw books the whole reward ungated, then autoAnnihilate with zero principal mints 100% of the backlog raw
classifiedFindings.function: autoAnnihilate (with withdraw as the enabling leg)
classifiedFindings.severityMove: DOWNGRADED from potential-medium to Low. Adjudicated, not deferred.
classifiedFindings.c4Criterion: State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments. Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges.
classifiedFindings.criterionQuoted: QA/Low: 'State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments.' The defect is that the code does not do what story-025 and CLAUDE.md say it does; it is not a Medium because no asset is at risk, no availability is impaired, and no value leaks.

classification.assetImpact: NONE incremental. Conservation is exact: owed == annihilatable + carried dust + raw-minted excess, verified independently by ECON-005 and by INV-1/INV-2 (PASS, MAX OBSERVED OVERSHOOT OVER THE EMISSION CEILING = 0 across 640,640 Foundry calls + 302,817 Medusa calls; the 1024-wei DUST_SLACK was never consumed). The bypass pays a staker exactly what claim() would have paid them and not one wei more. No over-emission, no dilution of other stakers, no principal-accounting breach (INV-3 PASS), no protocol funds moved.
classification.whatActuallyChanges: The DELIVERY FORM and the TIMING of the staker's own accrued Antimatter. story-025 intended a weeks-long 'teaching phase' during which reward could only be taken via autoAnnihilate (annihilated against principal); the bypass lets any staker take 100% raw to their wallet instead, immediately, for free, at any reward-to-principal ratio.
attackPath: 1. Staker calls withdraw(token, user.amount) -- UNGATED. :417-419 settles the entire pending reward into unclaimedReward and zeroes user.amount.

2. Staker calls autoAnnihilate(token, 0). principalAsAntimatter = user.amount * scale = 0 (:540), so capped -> 0 and netWanted -> 0; the annihilate block is skipped entirely and excessBase == the whole backlog.
3. :605 antimatter.mint(msg.sender, excess) delivers the full backlog raw. claim() is simultaneously reverting 'StableStaker: claim disabled'.
4. Optional re-stake. A PARTIAL withdraw tunes exactly how much is taken raw.
classification.likelihood: HIGH that it is used -- no special conditions, no capital, no MEV, no race, and it works on the wired direct ERC4626YieldStrategy with no round-trip haircut. Fuzzer-confirmed and shrunk to 1 call (INV-5 FAIL); deterministic replay Run17_ClaimGateBypass::test_twoTransactionsDrainTheWholeBacklogWithTheGateShut delivered 4166666666666666661600 wei = 10000 bps = 100% of entitlement. The ungated raw mint at :605 executed 13,630x under Medusa line coverage, so the path is not an artifact.
classification.assumptions: The staker is willing to unstake (forfeiting forward emission on that principal) for the duration. Nothing else.

classifiedFindings.justification: The mechanism is real, cheap, permissionless and fuzzer-proven, but its consequence does not reach the Medium bar on any of the three C4 limbs, and the PRIMARY ground for that is measured conservation -- not anything the owner says about the flag. Assets: none at risk. Conservation is exact (owed == annihilatable + carried dust + raw-minted excess) and Tier-3 measured ZERO overshoot over the emission ceiling across 640,640 Foundry calls + 302,817 Medusa calls (INV-1/INV-2 PASS; the 1024-wei DUST_SLACK was never consumed). The bypass pays a staker exactly what claim() would have paid them and not one wei more, so nothing is created, diluted or taken from another party (INV-3 PASS on principal accounting). The V2 premise that Antimatter is redeemable into UNBACKED phUSD bites only where INCREMENTAL Antimatter exists, and here none does: Antimatter.annihilate consumes the CALLER'S OWN stable half, so the bypass changes WHO sources the stable half and WHEN -- not WHETHER the resulting phUSD is backed. Availability: nothing is impaired; this is a path being MORE open than intended, not less. Value leak: there is none to leak -- the staker receives their own accrued entitlement. On the measurement alone no Medium limb is reached, and THAT is the ground of this Low: strike CLAUDE.md:184-203 from the record entirely and the Low still stands. The severity audit applied exactly that test. CORROBORATION, not the load-bearing ground: the protocol itself also declines to treat the gate as a boundary -- CLAUDE.md:184-203 says to 'read claimEnabled as a UX mechanism with a deliberate escape valve, NOT as an access control' and that 'nothing in the protocol's safety argument may depend on antimatter being unobtainable while the flag is false.' A control the owner has pre-committed to relying on for nothing cannot, when bypassed, impair protocol function -- but that disclaimer confirms the rating, it does not carry it. It is NOT a discount under N24 4(c): 4(c) forbids using the closed gate to LOWER some other finding's impact, and no such move is made here -- the reasoning runs the other way, from the owner's own refusal to depend on the gate to the absence of anything for the bypass to break. What the Low rating must NOT swallow, and what makes this the single most load-bearing Low in the run, is the FALSIFIED RATIONALE. The Auditor Note's bullet 2 -- 'the condition requires reward accrual to exceed staked principal, which at realistic emission rates takes a long time relative to how long the gate is intended to stay closed' -- is FALSE. It reasons only about organic accrual growing the numerator and never about a caller shrinking the denominator, which takes ONE ordinary transaction. story-025's Story Overview claim that autoAnnihilate 'becomes the only reward path' is likewise FALSE. Under the standing rule, a falsely-exhaustive doc RAISES severity rather than lowering it; here it raises this from an unremarkable spec note to a Low that must be read, because the owner will size the teaching phase and the rate of raw Antimatter entering circulation against a bound that does not exist. Reported at Low, but reported LOUDLY, and routed to spec-conformance as F-01 so it cannot be lost in a QA bundle.

footgun.surpriseTest: PASS -- a competent, non-malicious owner reading the Auditor Note believes the raw-mint path is rate-limited by an emission-vs-principal race and therefore negligible over a weeks-long gate. It is not rate-limited at all. Surprise => in scope.
footgun.safeConfigGuidance: Do not size the teaching phase, or any downstream expectation about circulating Antimatter, on the assumption that the gate throttles delivery. Treat claimEnabled as delivering ZERO throttle from day one. If a real throttle is wanted, gate the :605 raw-mint leg on the same flag (accepting that this re-strands the owed > principal user the Note was protecting), or accept the current behaviour and correct the documented bound.

law2Deviation.deviation: story-025 Story Overview (~line 15) states autoAnnihilate 'becomes the only reward path'. It is not. The Auditor Note's stated bound on the exception is factually false.
law2Deviation.storyState: auto-complete -- MACHINE approval, never human-reviewed; round 2 was rejected outright by its own reviewer (blocking [high]); every round ran --inline-delegation with self-declared 'Independence: reduced'. Worth stating to the owner alongside the finding.

classifiedFindings.n24_4c_compliance: COMPLIANT. No discount taken for the gate being closed. The Low rests on measured conservation and on the owner's own disclaimer of reliance, not on the gate's state.
notToBeOverstated: Do NOT describe this as over-minting, dilution, or theft. PATTERN-002's own harm (MINT-ON-DEMAND-OVERMINT) does NOT apply and the pattern-matcher flagged that verbatim.
Do NOT claim a broken access control. The project declares it is not one.
classifiedFindings.carryForward: During a pause of the FOREIGN Antimatter contract the ORDINARY reward path is dead (annihilate is whenNotPaused) but this bypass still works, because the zero-principal path skips the annihilate block and antimatter.mint is NOT whenNotPaused. A staker who knows the trick is unaffected; one who does not is locked out. State the asymmetry -- it is the argument against treating the bypass as an acceptable escape valve -- but do not rely on it as a mitigation.
classifiedFindings.flagReason: Borderline Low/Medium, adjudicated Low on measured conservation plus the owner's explicit non-reliance. A human who disagrees with the non-reliance disclaimer -- e.g. if any downstream phUSD-backing assumption turns out to depend on the teaching phase after all -- should re-weigh to Medium, and this classification should not stand in the way of that.
classifiedFindings.justificationOrdering: FINAL-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-09-01). Reordered so the Low rests on CONSERVATION as the primary ground (INV-1/INV-2 zero measured overshoot across ~943k calls; Antimatter.annihilate consumes the caller's own stable half, so backing is unchanged) with the owner's non-reliance disclaimer as CORROBORATION. Surviving test: strike CLAUDE.md:184-203 entirely and the Low still stands. The falsified story rationale is retained at full volume and is NOT suppressed.

classifiedFindings.title: The exit-shortfall floor is blind to a fee-charging ERC4626 vault: a 2-raw-unit + 1 bp allowance against a proportional shortfall means an external Tokemak fee crossing 1.00 bp bricks the only reward path
classifiedFindings.severityMove: UNCHANGED at Low. Explicitly NOT inflated to Medium, and explicitly NOT closed.
classifiedFindings.c4Criterion: State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments. Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges.
classifiedFindings.criterionQuoted: QA/Low today: the live-availability limb of Medium ('the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted') is REFUTED at HEAD by fresh measurement. It is retained as Low with an armed escalation trigger, not closed.

classification.assetImpact: None today. If the trigger fires: total loss of AVAILABILITY of the reward path (not of principal), because with claimEnabled false autoAnnihilate is the intended sole reward path, and every call above N = 2/(f - 1e-4) raw units would revert 'StableStaker: exit shortfall'.
attackPath: No attacker. The trigger is an EXTERNAL Tokemak governance parameter: the wired autopool's modeled exit discount f rising above EXACTLY 1.00 bp.
classification.likelihood: NOT LIVE. Fresh mainnet fork measurement THIS RUN (block 25878600, cold-cache re-fetched over RPC in 74.50s, numbers identical, 5/5 tests pass): autoDOLA 0.473049 bps, autoUSD 0.535370 bps -- BOTH below the 1 bp allowance, with no revert observed at ANY reward size on either pool. Halmos corroborates the boundary exactly: check_noBrick at 0 / 0.47 / 0.54 / 0.90 / 1.00-exact bp all PASS, check_crossing_101_hundredthsBp FAILS with a counterexample, and check_control_5bp FAILS as the POSITIVE CONTROL proving the harness can find the brick when one exists.
classification.assumptions: Wiring stays on autoDOLA / autoUSD. Both allowances are `constant` with NO setter, so if the trigger fires there is no parameter remedy -- only a redeploy or a fee-aware previewExitFor override in reflax-yield-vault, which does not exist at the pinned commit cdd0743.
classification.externalRequirements: A Tokemak-side fee change, entirely outside this protocol's control. The margin is 0.46-0.53 bp wide.

classifiedFindings.justification: The Medium case was refuted by measurement performed in this run against live mainnet state, not carried from a prior audit, and reproduced from a deleted cache -- so it is a real negative, not a stale one. Both wired autopools sit roughly 2x under the allowance and the PoC swept reward sizes without producing a single 'exit shortfall' revert. Reporting this as a live Medium would be exactly the overstatement the pipeline rejects. It stays open at Low for three reasons that survive the refutation and that the partial suppression under N18 does not reach: the deciding constants have NO setter and are not visible as configuration knobs, so an operator cannot respond if the trigger fires; nothing in the wiring runbook ties reward-path liveness to an EXTERNAL vault's fee parameter, so nobody is watching the 0.5 bp of headroom; and the revert string names the STRATEGY rather than the constant, pointing diagnosis at the wrong contract. The decimals cliff sharpens it -- the flat 2-unit allowance is worth 2e-6 USDC on a 6-decimal pool but 2e-18 DOLA on an 18-decimal pool, where the entire margin is the 1 bp. N18 legitimately suppresses the 'widen the allowance' remedy (the 1 bp figure was chosen deliberately below any real haircut, and INV-6's scaling law shows the flat 2 is load-bearing and must not be reduced); it says nothing about the monitoring gap or the misleading diagnostics, which is what remains.

escalationTrigger.condition: Wired autopool modeled exit discount f > 1.00 bp exactly.
escalationTrigger.escalatesTo: medium (availability of the sole reward path)
escalationTrigger.howToMonitor: Re-run reports/stable-staker/17/poc/Run17_ECON001_ExitFeeBrick.t.sol::test_measure_autopool_exit_haircut_bps against the live autopools. Pure measurement, needs no protocol state.
escalationTrigger.doNotClose: The trigger is an external parameter outside the protocol's control, so the finding must not be closed on the strength of today's measurement.

law2Deviation.deviation: story-025's own Review Failure Report 2026-08-31 (blocking [high]) demanded 'Re-derive the shortfall floor so a double-rounded-down ERC4626 delivery of amount - 1 (or a routine haircut) does not revert autoAnnihilate.' Round 3 satisfies the ROUNDING-scale criterion ONLY; Autonomous Decision 1 defers the fee case to a previewExitFor override in vault-RM that does not exist at the pinned commit. The round-3 regression fixture (MockERC4626Vault = OZ reference + donation hook) charges NO fee and is therefore structurally incapable of detecting the residual.

classifiedFindings.n24_4c_compliance: COMPLIANT. The closed gate is used only to establish that autoAnnihilate is the SOLE reward path (which RAISES the consequence if the trigger fires); it is not used to discount anything.
classifiedFindings.notOutOfScope: This is NOT the C4 fee-on-transfer-token exclusion. The fee is charged by a wired ERC4626 autopool on redemption, not by a token transfer hook.
classifiedFindings.crossRepo: Consumer side of reflax-yield-vault L-19 / 302656e234 and ECON-A / c50c08f9ee. Route, do not duplicate.

classifiedFindings.title: Dust-window liveness failure: a caller owed exactly 1 wei has netWanted == 1, convertToShares(1) == 0, and autoAnnihilate reverts 'StableStaker: exit shortfall', accusing an honest ERC4626 strategy of lying
classifiedFindings.c4Criterion: State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments. Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges.
classifiedFindings.criterionQuoted: QA/Low: 'State handling, function incorrect as to spec.' A transient, self-healing revert on a dust-sized request does not impair the function or availability of the protocol.

classification.assetImpact: None. Nothing is lost; the owed dust remains in unclaimedReward and the call succeeds once further accrual pushes owed above the boundary.
attackPath: No attacker. Ordinary state: caller owed a sub-share-price amount against a yielded vault (1.2467 assets/share in the counterexample); _disposeShares double-rounds down (ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:126-138), redeem delivers 0, require(received > 0) at :588 reverts.
classification.likelihood: OBSERVED at HEAD, 50 / 17,729 gate-closed attempts = 0.28%. 46 of the 50 landed on pool 1 (the REAL ERC4626YieldStrategy over a real OZ vault) and 0 on the idle pool. LOAD-BEARING: the fixture caveats disqualify only the FEE conclusions; the ROUNDING conclusions come from the real strategy. The 4 pool-2 hits are discounted as non-load-bearing.
classification.assumptions: Share price > 1 (i.e. the vault has yielded at all).

classifiedFindings.justification: This is the only one of the two floor findings that is actually happening at HEAD, and it is deliberately kept separate from CLASS-002 so that neither inherits the other's evidence status: CLASS-002 is refuted-but-armed and proportional, CLASS-003 is observed-and-live and integer, and they fail at opposite ends of the size axis with different remedies. It stays Low because it is self-healing -- the condition clears with further accrual, no value is destroyed and no path is permanently closed. The real cost is diagnostic: the revert message accuses an honest strategy of lying, and combined with CLASS-002's remedy note and CLASS-010's false-green view, an operator debugging a stuck reward path is pointed at the wrong contract three times over. The remedy is a dust short-circuit or a zero-shares pre-check in StableStakerV2; the flat EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE must NOT be raised for it, and must not be lowered either -- INV-6's scaling law (the floor fails whenever assetsPerShare > 2 + netFloor/10_000) shows the flat 2 is load-bearing, though it was demonstrated only at an unrealistic 1247 assets/share and is not itself a live finding at stablecoin-autopool prices.
classifiedFindings.n24_4c_compliance: COMPLIANT. No gate-based discount; the Low rests on self-healing and zero value impact.

classifiedFindings.title: story-025 creates a reward-forfeiture trap: underwater strategy plus drained buffer closes claim, autoAnnihilate and withdraw simultaneously, leaving only emergencyWithdraw, which zeroes unclaimedReward
classifiedFindings.severityMove: SETTLED at Medium (from potential-medium). Not raised to High.
classifiedFindings.c4Criterion: Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted, or leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements.
classifiedFindings.criterionQuoted: Medium: 'Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted, OR LEAK VALUE with a hypothetical attack path with STATED ASSUMPTIONS, but EXTERNAL REQUIREMENTS.' Both limbs are met: the reward surface is entirely unavailable in the trap state, and accrued, redeemable value is irreversibly destroyed on the only remaining exit.

classification.assetImpact: The staker's accrued unclaimedReward backlog is DESTROYED -- irreversibly, on-chain, with nothing minted. Tier-3 measured 4166666666666666650000 wei of Antimatter entitlement destroyed on the emergencyWithdraw path (:630 sets unclaimedReward[token][msg.sender] = 0 and never mints). Under the V2 premise that Antimatter is redeemable into unbacked phUSD via the permissionless Antimatter.annihilate, this is REAL USER VALUE, not opportunity cost: the project-wide minter-cushion and externally-derived-yield suppressions are VOID for V2 and are not available to soften this. Principal is unaffected.
attackPath: 1. The wired strategy goes below par (_isUnderwater true). Transient mean-reverting dips are the owner's own stated normal case for this buffer.
2. The shared idle buffer holds less than the staker's gross request. The buffer is WORKING CAPITAL, not a solvency reserve, so this is the EXPECTED state at scale, not an edge case.

3. claim reverts on claimEnabled (:440 -- the deployment default). withdraw reverts on the underwater guard (:423). autoAnnihilate passes guardUnderwater = true at :579 and reverts at _routeExit:1193. All four exits are shut except one.
4. The staker needing their principal calls emergencyWithdraw, the sole survivor; :630 zeroes the backlog and returns principal only. The reward is gone.

5. Race dynamic amplifies it: the buffer is FCFS (_routeExit:1188) and story-025 adds REWARD-seeking callers to a queue that previously held only PRINCIPAL-seeking callers, so the buffer exhausts sooner and the trap closes on LATER stakers first.
classification.likelihood: MEDIUM. Reachability is ONE condition, not two: the wired strategy goes below par. The second nominal condition -- an idle buffer short of the caller's gross request -- is the DEPLOYMENT DEFAULT, not a second conjunct. Verified in source: _routeDeposit:1139-1144 forwards 100% of every deposit to the strategy and retains nothing; setYieldStrategy:349-354 sweeps any idle balance INTO the strategy; and no donate / target-buffer / reserve mechanism exists anywhere in src/ (donateBuffer is harness-only, present in the test rig and not in production source). The PoC log records `idle buffer held by StableStakerV2: 0` after a 150,000-token stake into the real strategy. A non-zero idle balance can arise only from exit residue or an unmodelled owner set-aside. Underwater dips are the owner's own stated normal case for this buffer (69c7666eee triage). This places the finding at the TOP of the Medium band. It does not cross into High: no attacker, no theft, principal untouched, a wait-option survives, and one owner transaction defuses it. No attacker is required; the loss falls on an ordinary staker who needs their principal.
classification.assumptions: STATED: (i) strategy below par -- the ONLY genuine condition; (ii) idle buffer < the staker's gross request -- NOT an independent conjunct: it is the deployment default (see likelihood); (iii) claimEnabled false, which is also the deployment default; (iv) the staker's need for principal is time-sensitive enough that waiting for the dip to mean-revert or for owner intervention is not acceptable.
classification.externalRequirements: The strategy's underwater condition is driven by external market/AMM state. Full defusal is ONE owner transaction, setClaimEnabled(true), which is why this is not High.
classification.likelihoodCorrection: FINAL-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-09-01). The prior text read '... but the conjunction is a real gate and this classification does not assume the worst case.' That sentence is FACTUALLY FALSE and was removed, not softened: the buffer condition is the deployment default, so reachability collapses to the single condition that the strategy goes below par.

classifiedFindings.justification: This is the mirror image of CLASS-001 -- the same flag failing in the opposite direction -- and unlike CLASS-001 it destroys real value. It is NEW to this diff range: before story-025, claim() was ungated, so a trapped staker could claim first and THEN hatch out; the gate is precisely what converts a recoverable situation into a forced forfeiture, and Tier-3 measured what that costs. It is a Medium and not a High because no attacker steals anything, no protocol funds move to a third party, principal is untouched, the staker retains a wait-option, and a single owner transaction defuses it entirely. It is a Medium and not a Low because the value is real under the V2 Antimatter premise, the destruction is irreversible once the transaction lands, the trap state is reachable by ordinary market movement with no adversary, and the conditions that reach it are the conditions the buffer was built for. Two adjacent suppressions were correctly refused reach and this classification upholds both refusals: 0dca43f315 is `acknowledged` but concerns PRINCIPAL loss realisation, a different line and a different value at risk, in a state that did not exist when it was triaged; and N19's underwater carve-out cites as its authority a CLAUDE.md section, 'idle balance is automatically buffer', that DOES NOT EXIST in the file at HEAD -- it establishes intent only. N4 legitimately suppresses remedy (c): the forfeiture is the deliberate single rule of the escape hatch ('no reward, principal out') and recommending its removal would be a recommendation against documented intent. What N4 cannot reach, and what this Medium actually is, is the COERCION: N4's wording presupposes emergencyWithdraw is an escape hatch AMONG options, and an escape hatch that is the ONLY exit is not an escape hatch. Remedies (a) and (b) stand untouched.

footgun.surpriseTest: PASS -- CLAUDE.md anticipates EXACTLY this class for the ANTIMATTER PAUSE ('the owner flips claimEnabled to true for the duration of any antimatter pause') but does NOT anticipate it for the UNDERWATER case, which is the condition far more likely to occur. The operational obligation the design depends on is written down for the rarer trigger and unwritten for the common one. An owner who has read the two-pause-deadlock note reasonably believes they have enumerated the lockout conditions. They have not.
footgun.safeConfigGuidance: Preferred code remedy (a): exempt the reward-only leg from the underwater guard -- a caller whose netWanted is 0 moves no principal and has no reason to be blocked by a principal-solvency guard. Operational remedy (b) if (a) is deferred: extend the CLAUDE.md two-pause obligation to read 'the owner flips claimEnabled to true for the duration of any antimatter pause OR any period in which a wired strategy is underwater', and wire an alarm on _isUnderwater, since nothing on-chain enforces it. Do NOT rely on (c) -- N4 rules the forfeiture intentional.
footgun.notCentralization: This is classified by the impact it unlocks, not filed as a centralization or malicious-owner item. The owner does nothing wrong; the hazard is that a documented obligation has an unwritten branch.

classifiedFindings.n24_4c_compliance: COMPLIANT, AND LOAD-BEARING HERE. The obvious discount -- 'the owner can just open the gate, so it is Low' -- is exactly what 4(c) forbids, and it was NOT taken. The gate ships false and nothing on-chain reopens it.
adjacentEntriesNotMerged: 0dca43f315 (medium, acknowledged) -- PRINCIPAL loss realisation on emergencyWithdraw. Its acknowledgement is DENIED reach here: different line (:630 vs the share-redemption path), different value at risk, and the all-exits-closed state did not exist at triage time.

0651258fcc (low, open) -- describes where the forfeited value GOES (recycled to survivors via a stale index). Complementary: that entry is the destination, this one is why the user is FORCED onto the path.
e7065d7d58 (qa, open) -- same family (reward-path availability under a global flag), different mechanism.
classifiedFindings.pocStatus: DELIVERED -- nothing is owed. workspace/stable-staker/test/poc/Run17_M01_RewardForfeitureTrap.t.sol, 5/5 PASS, deterministic, no fork. Independently re-run and validated with a mutation test (inserting setClaimEnabled(true) and changing nothing else falsifies the headline assertion). Log: reports/stable-staker/17/poc/Run17_M01_RewardForfeitureTrap.out.txt. The Tier-3 measurement (4166666666666666650000 wei destroyed) corroborates it.
classifiedFindings.flagReason: Conditional Medium. If the owner judges the underwater + buffer-short conjunction to be operationally unreachable at the deployed buffer sizing, that is a triage decision to record on the entry -- not a reason to have rated it lower here.

poc.mutationTest: PASS -- setClaimEnabled(true) alone falsifies the headline assertion

classifiedFindings.title: Zero-principal backlog holder has NO reward path on a Migrating pool while claimEnabled is false -- and this is exactly the state DEDUP-001's bypass leaves behind
classifiedFindings.function: autoAnnihilate (reward-path availability on a Migrating pool)
classifiedFindings.c4Criterion: State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments. Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges.
classifiedFindings.criterionQuoted: QA/Low: 'State handling.' Availability is impaired for one user class, but the value SURVIVES and is recoverable, so the Medium limb is not reached.

classification.assetImpact: None destroyed. The backlog SURVIVES finalizeAndReset (which clears only migrationInfo and poolState). It is recoverable, but ONLY by an owner action -- setClaimEnabled(true) -- or by the pool being revived to Active.
attackPath: No attacker. A staker with user.amount == 0 and a non-zero unclaimedReward on a pool moved to Migrating matches none of the four paths: claim is blocked by the flag (:440, no PoolState gate); autoAnnihilate requires Active (:517); userMigrate requires amount > 0 (:866); emergencyWithdraw requires Active AND forfeits (:630).
classification.likelihood: LOW-MODERATE. Requires the conjunction of a fully-withdrawn-but-unclaimed position and a terminal migration. Note the coupling: this is PRECISELY the user state CLASS-001's bypass creates, so the two interact -- a staker who uses the bypass and is caught mid-migration is wedged. claim's own NatSpec at :435-437 names this exact user ('someone who fully withdrew and has not claimed yet'), so the class is known to the code's own author.
classification.assumptions: claimEnabled false (the deployment default) and the pool in terminal migration.

classifiedFindings.justification: Owner-recoverable with the value intact is the textbook Low. N9 correctly suppresses the sub-claim that blocking stake/withdraw/emergencyWithdraw during terminal migration is itself a defect -- migration is terminal by design and those blocks preserve the snapshot. What N9 does NOT reach, and what survives, is the DEAD END: N9 justifies blocking those three exits on the premise that a path remains open, and for this user story-025 has now closed the last one. Deliberately kept separate from CLASS-004: that one is the UNDERWATER state, ends in value DESTRUCTION and is remedied at :630; this one is the MIGRATING state, is recoverable and is remedied by a PoolState-aware gate. Different state, different outcome, different fix.

expiredClosure.entry: f1661ec524 (L-07, low, open, _exitPosition -- 'batchMigrate silently skips a zero-principal user holding an unclaimed backlog')

classifiedFindings.justification: Filed at Low as a DISCLOSURE, neither silently suppressed by the two prior wont-fix entries nor dishonestly re-filed as new. Hence the explicit naming. The re-file basis is narrow and stated honestly: the ONE new observation is THE RATE. autoAnnihilate consumes the grossed-up `gross` of buffer per unit of REWARD annihilated where withdraw requests exactly `amount` -- 1/(1-slip) times more buffer than the transaction economically needs -- and because claimEnabled ships false the caller cannot opt out by claiming instead. That bears directly on the owner's own 'daily-volume' sizing input quoted verbatim in 69c7666eee's triage: the buffer is sized for daily WITHDRAWAL volume, and story-025 adds a new, grossed-up, reward-driven draw to the same pool. N19 is the natural suppressor and is REFUSED: the section it cites as its authority does not exist in CLAUDE.md at HEAD, and its own text concedes '"the buffer is untouched" is a statement about the normal path, not an invariant of every call.' N20 is refused because it covers an extraction framing this finding explicitly does not make.
classifiedFindings.disposition: Attach as a Low ADDENDUM to 69c7666eee. It must NOT reopen either wont-fix on the merits; it should prompt the owner to re-check the buffer-sizing input. If triage disagrees, the correct outcome is wont-fix WITH the rate observation recorded on 69c7666eee -- never silent deletion.

newTriageItems.consequence: While a strategy is below par, withdraw is dead for EVERY staker, not merely for a staker whose request happens to exceed a partially-funded buffer. CLASS-004's availability limb is therefore BROADER than currently stated in the Medium report.
newTriageItems.action: Human decision: either (a) add a funding mechanism and make the buffer premise true, or (b) retract the buffer-sizing premise from N19 and from the 69c7666eee triage reason, and re-weigh CLASS-004's availability limb accordingly.
newTriageItems.doNot: Do not resolve this in-pipeline and do not use it to auto-escalate CLASS-004 this run.
